vsdh.shader.waiting: Activates when you leave the world
vsdh.shader.failed: Could not activate Vulkan shader pack
vsdh.shader.standard: Standard rendering without a shader pack
vsdh.options.shaderPack.tooltip: Shader pack from the "shaderpacks" folder. After "Apply" it is prepared and becomes active at once, also inside a world (the terrain is rebuilt). No restart needed. Not every pack is supported; if one fails, the current rendering stays and logs/latest.log has the reason.
vsdh.options.shaderProfile.tooltip: A preset the shader pack ships (for example LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH). "Pack default" uses the pack's own default values. Lower profiles run faster.
vsdh.options.shaderDistant.tooltip: On: the shader pack also lights and colours the distant Distant Horizons terrain when it ships programs for it. Off: distant terrain is drawn without the pack's programs.
vsdh.options.shaderFolder.tooltip: Opens the "shaderpacks" folder. Put the pack's ZIP file there unchanged and reopen these settings.
vsdh.shader.frameFailed: [VSDH] Shader pack stopped in this world (%s), standard rendering is active: %s
vsdh.shader.graphFailed: [VSDH] Shader pack could not be started here, standard rendering is active: %s
vsdh.shader.shadowReduced.details: Shadow resolution %s → %s to fit GPU memory
vsdh.options.shaderDistant.missing: Distant Horizons is not installed. VSDH also runs without DH; with DH it additionally draws the distant terrain.
vsdh.options.packOptions.none: First pick and apply a shader pack on the Shaders page
vsdh.options.packOptions.loading: Options appear once the selected pack has loaded
vsdh.options.packOptions.tooltip: Shader pack setting '%s'. After 'Apply' the pack reloads and becomes active at once, also inside a world. Choosing a new profile replaces individually changed options.
vsdh.options.packOptions.reset.tooltip: Sets every option back to the selected profile's value. Takes effect after 'Apply'; 'Undo' discards it.
vsdh.options.shaderStatus.tooltip: What is shown right now. A picked pack is prepared and then becomes active at once, also inside a world.
vsdh.options.framerateLimit.tooltip: Caps how many frames Minecraft renders each second. A sensible cap reduces GPU load, heat and power use; Max removes the cap. Against hitches: when graphics card and processor both run at their limit, single frames wait a long time for presentation. A cap slightly below your average FPS (or just below the monitor's refresh rate) removes most of these hitches.
vsdh.notice.unsupportedMods.title: VSDH: mods that are not fully supported
vsdh.notice.unsupportedMods.message: %s – display errors are possible. Nothing is blocked.
vsdh.notice.unsupportedMods.chat: [VSDH] These mods are not fully supported by the Vulkan renderer, display errors are possible: %s. Nothing is blocked.
vsdh.options.windowMode.tooltip: Controls how Minecraft uses the display: a window, or exclusive fullscreen at the chosen resolution and refresh rate.
